plain_english: Arjuna said: O mighty-armed one, O Hṛṣīkeśa, O Kesi-slayer, I desire to know separately the truth of renunciation and of abandonment. You previously said that the renouncer is wise, and that the ascetic and yogi are not fireless, and so on. Thus, hearing of these two renouncers, this question arises for one who wishes to know their distinction; here is the answer.
sanskrit_cite: atha aṣṭadaśo'dhyāyaḥ   arjuna uvāca   saṃnyāsasya mahābāho tattvamicchāmi veditum | tyāgasya ca  hṛṣīkeśa pṛthakkeśiniṣūdana | pūrvamuktaṃ sa tyāgī sa ca buddhimān iti | tathā sa saṃnyāsī ca  yogī ca na niragniḥ ityādi | atastyāgisaṃnyāsinordvayoḥ  śravaṇāt viśeṣajijñāsorayaṃ praśnaḥ | atrottaraṃ-

plain_english: The blessed Lord said: the wise know renunciation of desired actions as complete renunciation; the discerning call renunciation of all action-fruits renunciation. Desired rites such as agniṣṭoma are all actions; for all nitya and naimittika actions, even while being performed, renunciation of the fruit is renunciation. What remains to be spoken in this chapter was expanded and examined by ancients such as Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara; for those whose essence is fulfilling the promise of merely clarifying hidden meaning, what is the effort of showing repetition? Here, for determining the distinction, opinions are presented.
sanskrit_cite: śrībhagavānuvāca   kāmyānāṃ karmaṇāṃ tyāgaṃ saṃnyāsaṃ kavayo viduḥ | sarvakarmaphalatyāgaṃ prāhustyāgaṃ vicakṣaṇāḥ | kāmyāni-agniṣṭomādīni | sarvakarmeti | sarveṣāṃ-nityanaimittika-karmaṇāṃ kriyamāṇatve'pi  phalatyāgastyāgaḥ | atra cādhyāye yadavaśiṣṭaṃ vaktavyamasti  tatprāktanaireva tatrabhavadbhaṭṭabhāskarādibhirvitatya  vimṛṣṭamiti kimasmākaṃ  tadgūḍhārthaprakāśanamātrapratijñānirvāhaṇasārāṇāṃ  punaruktapradarśanaprayāsena | tadatraiva viśeṣanirṇayāya matānyupanyasyati-

plain_english: Some say all action is defective and should be abandoned; others say sacrifice, charity, and austerity should not. Some distinguish by good fruit; others, like Sāṃkhya/Grhya followers, reject action tainted by violence and sin. Mīmāṃsakas hold sacrifice has a purpose known from scripture. Thus Vedic violence is not mere violence, and general prohibitions are overridden in that context; hawk-sacrifice violence pertains to fruit and meditative cognition. The learned therefore do not abandon sacrifices and similar rites even when joined with violence, since scripture alone distinguishes duty from non-duty.
sanskrit_cite: tyājyaṃ doṣavadityeke karma prāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ | yajñadānatapaḥkarma na tyājyamiti cāpare | doṣavat-hiṃsādimattvātpāpayuktam | tatkarma tyājyaṃ (na sarvaṃ  śubhaphalam)-iti kecittyāge viśeṣaṃ manyante sāṃkhyagṛhyā iva | anye tu-mīmāṃsākañcukānupraviṣṭā kratvartho hi  śāstrādavagamye iti | tathā tasmādyā vaidikī hiṃsā * * * * * | ityādinayenetikartavyatāṃśabhāginī (hiṃsā) hiṃsaiva na bhavati  na hiṃsyāt iti sāmānyaśāstrasya tatra bādhanāt | śyenādyeva tu  hiṃsā | phalāṃśe bhāvanāyāśca pratyayo'nuvidhāyakaḥ (ślo0 vā0)   ityanyān yajñādīn hiṃsādiyogino'pi na tyajet | śāstraikaśaraṇakāryākāryavibhāgāḥ paṇḍitā iti manyante

plain_english: Hear my determination about renunciation, best of the Bharatas; renunciation is indeed declared threefold, O tiger among men.
sanskrit_cite: niścayaṃ śṛṇu me tatra tyāge bharatasattama | tyāgo hi  puruṣavyāghra trividhaḥ samprakīrtitaḥ

plain_english: Sacrifice, gift, austerity, and action should not be abandoned; they must indeed be done. Sacrifice, gift, and austerity are purifiers for the wise.
sanskrit_cite: yajñadānatapaḥkarma na tyājyaṃ kāryameva tat | yajño dānaṃ  tapaścaiva pāvanāni manīṣiṇām

plain_english: Even these actions should be performed, abandoning attachment and their fruits; this is my certain supreme opinion, O Pārtha.
sanskrit_cite: etānyapi ca karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā phalāni ca | kartavyānīti me  pārtha niścitaṃ matamuttamam

plain_english: Renunciation of fixed action is unfit; abandonment from delusion is declared dark.
sanskrit_cite: niyatasya ca saṃnyāsaḥ karmaṇo nopapadyate | mohāttasya  parityāgastāmasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ

plain_english: Who abandons action as pain from fear of bodily distress performs rajas abandonment and obtains no fruit of abandonment.
sanskrit_cite: duḥkhamityeva yaḥ karma kāyakleśabhayāt tyajet | sa kṛtvā  rājasaṃ tyāgaṃ naiva tyāgaphalaṃ labhet

plain_english: Fixed duty done while abandoning attachment and fruit is considered sattva abandonment.
sanskrit_cite: kāryamityeva yatkarma niyataṃ kriyate'rjuna | saṅgaṃ tyaktvā  phalaṃ caiva sa tyāgaḥ sāttviko mataḥ

plain_english: A renouncer filled with sattva, wise and doubt-cut, neither hates unskillful action nor attaches to skillful action.
sanskrit_cite: na dveṣṭyakuśalaṃ karma kuśale nānuṣajjate | tyāgī  sattvasamāviṣṭo medhāvī chinnasaṃśayaḥ

plain_english: Since embodied beings cannot abandon all actions, one who abandons action-fruit is called a renouncer; true abandonment performs actions equally without attachment, aversion, or fruit-desire.
sanskrit_cite: nahi dehabhṛtā śakyaṃ tyaktuṃ karmāṇyaśeṣataḥ | yastu  karmaphalatyāgī sa tyāgītyabhidhīyate | tatra tvayaṃ  niścayaḥ-prāglakṣitaguṇasvarūpavaicitryāttyāgasyaiva  sattvarajastamomayyā cittavṛttyā kriyamāṇasya  tadviśiṣṭasvabhāvāvabhāsivastusthityā tyāgo  nāma-parabrahmavidāṃ siddhyasiddhyādiṣu samatayā  rāgadveṣaparihāreṇa phalaprepsāviraheṇa karmaṇāṃ nirvartanam | ata evāha-rājasaṃ tāmasaṃ ca tyāgaṃ kṛtvā na  kaścitphalasaṃbandhaḥ iti | sāttvikasya tu tyāgāt  śāstrārthapālanātmakaṃ phalam | tyaktaguṇagrāmagrahasya  punarmuneḥ satyatastyāgavācoyuktirupapattimatī

plain_english: Threefold fruit of action comes to non-renouncers after death, never to renouncers; ignorant men, though causes stand, impose the whole burden of agency on the self and bind themselves by their own intellect, not by thing-state.
sanskrit_cite: aniṣṭamiṣṭaṃ miśraṃ ca trividhaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam | bhavatyatyāgināṃ pretya na tu saṃnyāsināṃ kvacit | atyāginām-phalamayānām | adhunā vyavahāradaśāyāmapi pañcasvapi karmahetuṣu sthiteṣu  balādevāmī avidyāndhāḥ pumāṃsaḥ svātmanyeva  sakalakartṛbhāvabhāramāropayanti | ato nijayaiva dhiyātmānaṃ  badhnanti natu vastusthityā asya bandhaḥ-ityupadiśyate-

plain_english: O mighty-armed, know from me these five causes spoken in settled doctrine for the success of all actions.
sanskrit_cite: pañcemāni mahābāho kāraṇāni nibodha me | sāṅkhye kṛtānte  proktāni siddhaye sarvakarmaṇām | kṛto'nto niścayo yatreti kṛtāntaḥ-siddhāntaḥ

plain_english: Basis, agent, instrument, various separate efforts, and divine are the five factors here.
sanskrit_cite: adhiṣṭhānaṃ tathā kartā karaṇaṃ ca pṛthagvidham | vividhāśca  pṛthakceṣṭā daivamevātra pañcamam

plain_english: Whatever action one begins by body, speech, or mind, right or opposite, these five are its causes.
sanskrit_cite: śarīravāṅmanobhirhi yatkarmārabhate'rjuna | nyāyyaṃ vā  viparītaṃ vā pañcaite tasya hetavaḥ

plain_english: Thus being so, one who sees only himself as agent, not seeing the five factors, is evil-minded.
sanskrit_cite: tatraivaṃ sati kartāramātmānaṃ kevalaṃ tu yaḥ | paśyatyakṛtabuddhitvānna sa paśyati durmatiḥ

plain_english: One whose state is not ego-made and whose intellect is unstained is not bound even by killing.
sanskrit_cite: yasya nāhaṃkṛto bhāvo buddhiryasya na lipyate | hatvāpi sa  imāṁllokānna hanti na nibadhyate | adhiṣṭhānam-viṣayaḥ | daivam-prāgarjitaṃ śubhāśubham | pañcaite adhiṣṭhānā-dayaḥ sāmagrīrūpatāṃ prāptāḥ  sarvakarmasu hetavaḥ | anye tu adhiṣṭhīyate anena sarvaṃ karmeti  buddhigataṃ rajo labdhavṛttikaṃ  dhṛtiśraddhāsukhavividiṣāvividiṣārūpapañcakapariṇāmikarmayoga  śabda-vācyamadhiṣṭhānaṃ kvacitprayatnaśabdenoktam | kartā-anusandhātā buddhilakṣaṇaḥ | karaṇam-manaścakṣurādi  bāhyamapi ca khaḍgādi | ceṣṭāprāṇāpānādikā | daivaśabdena  dharmādharmau | tābhyāṃ ca buddhigatāḥ sarve'pi bhāvā  upalakṣitāḥ | anye tvadhiṣṭhānamīśvaraṃ  manyante-akṛtabuddhitvādaniścitaprajñatayā | yaḥ  punarahaṃkāraviyogadārḍhyena prāguktayuktiśataśodhitena karmāṇi  karoti na sa bandhabhāk-kṛtabuddhitvādityāśayaḥ

plain_english: Knowledge, knowable, and knower form a threefold impulsion of action; instrument, action, and agent form its gathering.
sanskrit_cite: jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ parijñātā trividhā karmacodanā | karaṇaṃ karma  karteti trividhaḥ karmasaṃgrahaḥ | karmaṇi codanā-pravṛttīcchā | tatsamaye  yeṣāmabodhamātraniṣṭhatvājjñānajñeyajñātṛśrutivācyatā  teṣāmeva samyaggrahaṇarūpaṃ yatphalābhisaṃdhānenātmīyabuddhyā  svīkaraṇam-ahametadbhokṣye yato mayā kṛtam-ityevaṃrūpam tatsamaye  tathā nirvartanāvasare  karaṇakarmakartṛśabdāmidheyatvamāviṣṭatvāt | ato yogināmāveśo  nāstīti tānprati karaṇādigirāṃ prasaṅgo nāsti apitu  jñānamātre eva tātparyam | athaiṣāṃ ṣaṇṇāmapi saṃkṣepeṇa guṇabhedādbhedaṃ  darśayitumāha-

plain_english: Knowledge, action, and agent are each declared threefold by strand-difference; hear them properly as the text enumerates their forms.
sanskrit_cite: jñānaṃ karma ca kartā ca tridhaiva guṇabhedataḥ | procyate  guṇasaṅkhyāne yathāvacchṛṇu tānyapi | guṇānāṃ saṃkhyānaṃ-niścayo yatra tatra sāṃkhyīyakṛtānte  jñānādi trividhamucyate yattacchṛṇviti saṃgatiḥ | jñānam-ityanena jñāne kriyāyāṃ ca yatkaraṇaṃ taddvividhamuktam | evaṃ karmeti jñeyaṃ kāryaṃ ca | jñātā kartā ceti | tatra sarvabhūteṣu ityādinā ślokatrayeṇa jñānakaraṇasya  trairūpyamuktam | ata eva yena-iti tṛtīyā | iyatā ca  jñānakaraṇasāmānyasya svarūpamuktam | niyatam ityādinā  ślokatrayeṇa karmaṇo jñeyakāryarūpasya dvaividhyam | muktasaṅgaḥ  ityādinā ślokatrayeṇa tu karturdvirūpasya saṃkṣepeṇa svarūpam | karaṇaviśeṣasya svarūpabhedapratipādanārthaṃ buddhestraividhyaṃ  nirūpitam tadvāreṇa karaṇāntarāṇāmapi traividhyamupalakṣitam | karaṇasya tvitikartavyatāpekṣitvāditikartavyatāyāśca  dhṛtyādipañcakarūpatve'pi śraddhāyāḥ

plain_english: Know that knowledge as sattvic which sees one imperishable being, undivided, among divided beings such as gods and men.
sanskrit_cite: pūrvamuktatvādvividiṣāvividiṣayośca  dhṛtisukhābhyāmākṣepāttayostraividhyaṃ dhṛtyā yayā ityanena  sukhaṃ tvidānīm-ityanena coktam | tadāha   sarvabhūteṣu yenaikaṃ bhāvamavyayamīkṣate | avibhaktaṃ  vibhakteṣu tajjñānaṃ viddhi sāttvikam | vibhakteṣu-devamanuṣyāditayā

plain_english: But knowledge that knows many various beings as separate in all beings is remembered as rajasic, through an intellect of my pleasure and my hatred.
sanskrit_cite: pṛthaktvena tu yajjñānaṃ nānābhāvān pṛthagvidhān | vetti  sarveṣu bhūteṣu tadrājasamiti smṛtam | pṛthaktvena-iha me prītiriha me dveṣaḥ-ityādibuddhyā

plain_english: But knowledge attached to one task as a whole, causeless and small in true meaning, is called tamasic, arising from obsession and grasping anger and attachment.
sanskrit_cite: yattu kṛtsnavadekasminatkārye saktamahetukam | atattvārthavadalpaṃ  ca tattāmasamudāhṛtam | ahetukam-kāraṇamavicāryaiva abhiniveśāveśavaśāt  krodharāgādigrahaṇaṃ yattattāmasasaṃjñam

plain_english: Action that is fixed, done without attachment and aversion, by one not desiring fruit, is called sattvic.
sanskrit_cite: niyataṃ saṅgarahitamarāgadveṣataḥ kṛtam | aphalaprepsunā karma  yattat sāttvikamucyate | niyatam-kartavyamiti

plain_english: But action done by one seeking desire, with ego, again and again, abundant in suffering and pervaded by ignorance and the rest, is remembered as rajasic.
sanskrit_cite: yattu kāmepsunā karma sāhaṅkāreṇa vā punaḥ | kriyate  kleśabahulaṃ tadrājasamiti smṛtam | kleśaiḥ-avidyādyaiḥ bahulam-vyāptam

plain_english: Action begun from delusion, without considering consequence, destruction, violence, or manly effort, is called tamasic.
sanskrit_cite: anubandhaṃ kṣayaṃ hiṃsāmanavekṣya ca pauruṣam | mohādārabhyate  karma yattattāmasamucyate | mohāt-abhiniveśamayāt

plain_english: The agent free from attachment, endowed with steadfastness and zeal, unchanged in success or failure, is called sattvic; he does not say 'I am the doer,' yet even a yogi's conventional speech 'I do' is not forbidden.
sanskrit_cite: muktasaṅgo'nahaṃvādī dhṛtyutsāhasamanvitaḥ | siddhyasiddhyornirvikāraḥ kartā sāttvika ucyate | ahaṃ kartā iti na vadan tacchīlastaddharmā tatsādhukārī vā yo  bhavatīti-anahaṃvādī-ityanena ṇininā  vyavahāramātrasaṃvṛtivaśena yogino'pi ahaṃ karomi-iti vaco na  niṣiddham

plain_english: The attached agent who desires fruit, is greedy, violent, impure, and joined with joy and sorrow in success and failure, is called rajasic.
sanskrit_cite: rāgī karmaphalaprepsurlubdho hiṃsātmako'śuciḥ | harṣaśokānvitaḥ kartā rājasaḥ parakīrtyate | harṣaśokānvitaḥ-siddhyasiddhyoḥ

plain_english: The undisciplined, ordinary, stiff, deceitful, cruel, lazy, despondent, and procrastinating agent is called tamasic.
sanskrit_cite: ayuktaḥ prākṛtaḥ stabdhaḥ śaṭho naiṣkṛtiko'lasaḥ | viṣādī  dīrghasūtraśca kartā tāmasa ucyate | nikṛtiḥ-nairghṛṇyam

plain_english: Hear completely and separately, Arjuna, the threefold distinction of intellect and steadfastness by the strands: intellect is decision, steadfastness is contentment; whatever good or bad is done is necessarily done, and steadfastness exists in all.
sanskrit_cite: buddherbhedaṃ dhṛteścaiva guṇatastrividhaṃ śṛṇu | procyamānamaśeṣeṇa pṛthaktvena dhanañjaya | buddhiḥ-niścayaḥ | dhṛtiḥ-santoṣaḥ | sarvo hi sukṛtaṃ  duṣkṛtaṃ vā kṛtvā ante avaśyaṃ kṛtaṃ karaṇīyaṃ  kimanyena-iti dhiyaṃ gṛhṇāti | anyathā kriyābhyo vyuparame ko  hetuḥ syāt | ataḥ sarvasyaiva dhṛtirastīti tātparyārthaḥ | padārthastvaprasiddho vyākhyāyata eva

plain_english: The intellect that knows activity and withdrawal, duty and non-duty, fear and fearlessness, bondage and liberation, is considered sattvic, Arjuna.
sanskrit_cite: pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca kāryākārye bhayābhaye | bandhaṃ  mokṣaṃ ca yā buddhirveda sā pārtha sātvakī matā

plain_english: The intellect by which one improperly knows right and wrong, duty and non-duty, is rajasic, O Pārtha.
sanskrit_cite: yayā dharmamadharmaṃ ca kāryaṃ cākāryameva ca | ayathāvat  prajānāti buddhiḥ sā pārtha rājasī | ayathāvat-asamyak

plain_english: The intellect joined with darkness, which understands wrong as right and reverses all meanings, is considered tamasic.
sanskrit_cite: adharmaṃ dharmamiti yā buddhyate tamasānvitā | sarvārthānviparītāṃśca buddhiḥ sā tāmasī matā

plain_english: Steadfastness by which, through unwavering yoga, one holds mind, breath, and sense actions, is sattvic; thinking 'may I become self-delighting in every way,' one restrains them by yoga.
sanskrit_cite: dhṛtyā mayā dhārayate manaḥprāṇendriyakriyāḥ | yogenāvyabhicāriṇyā dhṛtiḥ sā sāttvikīmatā | manaḥprāṇendriyakriyāḥ yogena dhārayati yatā kiṃ  mamopabhogādibhiḥ sarvathaivātmārāmo bhūyāsam-iti manvānaḥ

plain_english: But steadfastness by which one holds duty, desire, and wealth, O Arjuna, with attachment and fruit-desire, is rajasic, O Pārtha; not by mere attachment but by such fixation.
sanskrit_cite: yayā tu dharmakāmārthāndhṛtyā dhārayate'rjuna | prasaṅgena  phalākāṃkṣī dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha rājasī | prasaṅgeneti-na tathābhiniveśena

plain_english: Steadfastness by which the dull-minded one does not release sleep, fear, grief, despair, and delusion is tamasic; by which one binds contentment to those states, that too is tamasic steadfastness.
sanskrit_cite: yayā svapnaṃ bhayaṃ śokaṃ viṣādaṃ mohameva ca | na vimuñcati  durmedhā dhṛtiḥ sā tāmasī matā | nidrākalahādiṣveva yayā santoṣaṃ badhnāti tatparatayā-sā  tāmasī dhṛtiḥ

plain_english: But now hear from me, O bull of the Bharatas, the threefold happiness, where one delights through practice and reaches the end of suffering.
sanskrit_cite: sukhaṃ tvidānīṃ trividhaṃ śṛṇu me bharatarṣabha | abhyāsādramate yatra duḥkhāntaṃ ca nigacchati

plain_english: That happiness which is sattvic is at first like poison but in the end like nectar; it is born from the clarity of self and mind, and at first practice it is hard to remove like poison because of long habituated attachment to objects, as scripture says the razor's edge is difficult to cross; mind-clarity arises from self-clarity because no other is needed.
sanskrit_cite: yattadāttve viṣamiva pariṇāme'mṛtopamam | tatsukhaṃ sāttvikaṃ  vidyādātmabuddhiprasādajam | tadātve-abhyāsakāle | viṣamiva-janmaśatābhyastaviṣayasaṅgasya  duṣpariharatvāt | uktaṃ ca śrutau-   kṣurasya dhārā viṣamā duratyayā | ityādi | ātmaprasādādbuddhiprasādo  jāyate-anyasyāpekṣyamāṇasyābhāvāt

plain_english: That happiness which is from contact of objects and senses is at first like nectar but in the end like poison; it is called rajasic, born from mutual contact of objects and senses, like the eye's connection with form.
sanskrit_cite: viṣayendriyasaṃyogādyattadagre'mṛtopamam | pariṇāme viṣamiva tat  rājasamiti smṛtam | viṣayendriyāṇāṃ parasparasaṃyogajaṃ sukham cakṣuṣa iva  rūpasaṃbandhāt

plain_english: That happiness which at first and in continuation deludes the self, arising from sleep, laziness, and carelessness, is called tamasic; from sleep, by laziness and carelessness, as explained before, that happiness is tamasic.
sanskrit_cite: yadagre cānubandhe ca sukhaṃ mohanamātmanaḥ | nidrālasyapramādotthaṃ tattāmasamudāhṛtam | nidrātaḥ-ālasyena pramādena pūrvaṃ vyākhyātena yatsukhaṃ  tattāmasam

plain_english: No being on earth, in heaven, or among gods is free from the three strands; action, knowledge, and happiness are analyzed through their mutual relations, and the one abiding in sattvic wealth is fit for knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: na tadasti pṛthivyāṃ vā divi deveṣu vā punaḥ | sattvaṃ  prakṛtijairmuktaṃ yadebhiḥ syāttribhirguṇaiḥ | evaṃ kartṛkarmakaraṇānāṃ buddhidhṛtyoḥ sukhasya ca  sattvādibhedabhinnānāṃ  parasparāṅgāṅgibhāvabādhyabādhakatvasamuccayādvṛttikramayaugapa  dyādi-yogādaparisaṃkhyeyabhedatvādvividhaphalaprasavasamarthatvam | ityanena karmaṇāṃ prāk sūtritaṃ gahanatvaṃ vitatya sahetukaṃ  nirṇītam | sarve caite devatādisthāvarāntā guṇatrayasaṃbandhaṃ  nātikrāmanti | uktaṃ hi   ā brahmaṇaśca kīṭāntaṃ na kaścittattvataḥ sukhī | karoti  vikṛtīstāstāḥ sarva eva jijīviṣuḥ | iti | tattvato hi sukhaṃ guṇātikrāntamanasaḥ netarasyetyāśayaḥ | evamiyatā ṣaṇṇāṃ pratyekaṃ trisvarūpatvaṃ dhṛtyādīnāṃ ca  pratipāditam | tanmadhyātsāttvike rāśau vartamāno daivīṃ  sampadaṃ prāpta iha jñāne yogyaḥ tvaṃ ca tathāvidhaḥ-ityarjunaḥ  protsāhitaḥ | adhunā tvidamucyate-yadi tāvadanayā jñānabuddhyā  karmaṇi bhavānpravartate tadā svadharmapravṛttyā  vijñānapūtatayā ca na karmasaṃbandhastava | athaitannānumanyase  tadavaśyaṃ tava pravṛttyā tāvadbhāvyam jātereva tathābhāve  sthitatvāt | yataḥ sarvaḥ svabhāvaniyataḥ  kutaściddoṣāttirohitatatsvabhāvaḥ kañcitkāla bhūtvāpi

plain_english: When concealment disappears, nature manifests; caste natures necessarily act, and actions are divided by nature-born strands.
sanskrit_cite: tattirodhāyakavigame svabhāvaṃ vyaktāpannaṃ labhata eva | tathāhyevaṃvidho varṇānāṃ svabhāvaḥ | evamavaśyaṃ bhāvinyāṃ  pravṛttau tataḥ phalavibhāgitā bhavet-tadāha   brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ ca parantapa | karmāṇi  pravibhaktāni svabhāvaprabhavairguṇaiḥ

plain_english: Calmness, self-control, purity, patience, straightness, knowledge, discernment, and theism are brahmin nature-born action.
sanskrit_cite: śamo damastathāḥ śaucaṃ kṣāntirārjavameva ca | jñānaṃ  vijñānamāstikyaṃ brāhmaṃ karma svabhāvajam

plain_english: Heroism, splendor, steadiness, skill, not fleeing in battle, generosity, and lordliness are kshatriya action born of nature.
sanskrit_cite: śauryaṃ tejo dhṛtirdākṣyaṃ yuddhe cāpyapalāyanam | dānamīśvarabhāvaśca kṣātraṃ karma svabhāvajam

plain_english: Farming, cattle protection, and trade are vaishya duty; service-based action is shudra duty, both born of nature.
sanskrit_cite: kṛṣigorakṣyavāṇijyaṃ vaiśyakarma svabhāvajam | payutthānātmakaṃ karma śūdrasyāpi svabhāvajam

plain_english: A person engaged in his own duty obtains perfection; devoted to his own work he finds success; hear that.
sanskrit_cite: sve sve karmaṇyabhirataḥ saṃsiddhiṃ labhate naraḥ | svakarmanirataḥ siddhiṃ yathā vindati tacchṛṇu

plain_english: From whom beings originate and by whom all this is pervaded, a human worshipping him through his own action finds success.
sanskrit_cite: yataḥ pravṛttirbhūtānāṃ yena sarvamidaṃ tatam | svakarmaṇā  tamabhyarcya siddhiṃ vindati mānavaḥ

plain_english: One's own duty, though deficient, is better than another's duty well performed; doing nature-fixed action one does not incur sin.
sanskrit_cite: śreyānsvadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmātsvanuṣṭhitāt | svabhāvaniyataṃ karma kurvannāpnoti kilviṣam

plain_english: Kaunteya, one should not abandon innate action even if faulty, for all beginnings are covered by fault like fire by smoke.
sanskrit_cite: sahajaṃ karma kaunteya sadoṣamapi na tyajet | sarvārambhā hi  doṣeṇa dhūmenā'gnirivāvṛtāḥ

plain_english: One with unattached mind, self-conquered and free from desire, attains supreme perfection of inaction through renunciation.
sanskrit_cite: asaktabuddhiḥ sarvatra jitātmā vigataspṛhaḥ | naiṣkarmyasiddhiṃ  paramāṃ saṃnyāsenādhigacchati

plain_english: As one who has attained perfection reaches brahman, so know from me in brief, O son of Kunti, the supreme steadfastness of knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: siddhiṃ prāpto yathā brahma tathāpnoti nibodha me | samāsene tu  kaunteya niṣṭhā jñānasya yā parā

plain_english: Joined with purified intellect, restraining the self by firmness, abandoning sound and other objects, and casting away attachment and aversion.
sanskrit_cite: buddhyā viśuddhayā yukto dhṛtyātmānaṃ niyamya ca | śabdādīnviṣayāṃstyaktvā rāgadveṣau vyudasya ca

plain_english: Dwelling in seclusion, eating lightly, restraining speech, body, and mind, devoted to meditation yoga, always taking refuge in dispassion.
sanskrit_cite: viviktasevī laghvāśī yatavākkāyamānasaḥ | dhyānayogaparo  nityaṃ vairāgyaṃ samupāśritaḥ

plain_english: Having released ego, strength, pride, desire, anger, and possession, free from mine-ness and peaceful, one becomes fit for brahman-becoming.
sanskrit_cite: ahaṅkāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ parigraham | vimucya  nirmamaḥ śānto brahmabhūyāya kalpate

plain_english: Becoming brahman, with clear self, one neither grieves nor rejoices, is equal toward all beings, and obtains supreme devotion to me.
sanskrit_cite: brahmabhūtaḥ prasannātmā na śocati na hṛṣyati | samaḥ sarveṣu  bhūteṣu madbhaktiṃ labhate parām

plain_english: By devotion one truly knows me, and having truly known me, enters into me thereafter.
sanskrit_cite: bhaktyā māmabhijānāti yo'haṃ yaścāsmi tattvataḥ | tato māṃ  tattvato jñātvā viśate tadanantaram

plain_english: Doing all actions always while taking refuge in me, one obtains the eternal imperishable station by my grace.
sanskrit_cite: sarvakarmāṇyapi sadā kurvāṇo madvyapāśrayaḥ | matprasādādavāpnoti śāśvataṃ padamavyayam

plain_english: Dedicating all actions to me by mind, O Bharata, taking refuge in discernment-yoga, be always of mind fixed on me.
sanskrit_cite: cetasā sarvakarmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya bhārata | buddhiyogaṃ  samāśritya maccittaḥ satataṃ bhava

plain_english: With mind fixed on me you will cross all difficulties by my grace; but if you refuse from ego, you will not be freed and will perish.
sanskrit_cite: maccittaḥ sarvadurgāṇi matprasādāttariṣyasi | atha  cettvamahaṅkārāṃ na mokṣyasi vinaṃkṣyasi

plain_english: Thinking 'relying on ego I will not fight' is false; your resolve is false, and nature will compel you.
sanskrit_cite: yadahaṅkāramāśritya na yotsya iti manyase | mithyaipa vyavasāyaste  prakṛtistvāṃ niyokṣyati

plain_english: Bound by innate nature to action, one must perform actions with my declared knowledge as authority; then bondage ceases.
sanskrit_cite: svabhāvajena kaunteya nibaddhaḥ svena karmaṇā | kartuṃ necchasi  yanmohātkariṣyasyavaśo'pi tat | brāhmaṇādīnāṃ karmapravibhāganirūpaṇasya svabhāvo'vaśyaṃ  nātikrāmatīti kṣatriyasvabhāvasya bhavato'nicchato'pi prakṛtiḥ  svabhāvākhyā niyoktṛtāmavyabhicāreṇa bhajate | kevalaṃ tayā  niyuktasya puṇyapāpasaṃbandhaḥ | ato  madabhihitavijñānapramāṇapuraḥsarīkāreṇa karmāṇyanutiṣṭha | tathā sati bandho nivartsyati | ityasyārthasya  parikarabandhaghaṭanatātparyaṃ mahāvākyārthasya | avāntaravākyānāṃ spaṣṭārthaḥ | samāsena saṃkṣepeṇa  jñānasya prāguktasya | niṣṭhāṃ vāgjālaparihāreṇa  niścitāmāha-buddhyā viśuddhayā-ityādi | sarvametadvyākhyātaprāyamiti na punarāyasyate

plain_english: The Lord dwells in the heart of all beings and whirls them, mounted on the machine of maya.
sanskrit_cite: īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ hṛdyeṣa vasate'rjuna | bhrāmayansarvabhūtāni yantrārūḍhāni māyayā

plain_english: Go to that very refuge with whole being; by his grace you will obtain the eternal place.
sanskrit_cite: tameva śaraṇaṃ gaccha sarvabhāvena bhārata | tatprasādātparāṃ  sidiṃ sthānaṃ prāpsyasi śāśvatam | eṣa īśvaraḥ paramātmāvaśyaṃ śaraṇatvena grāhyaḥ | tatra  hyadhiṣṭhātari kartari boddhari svātmamaye vimṛṣṭe na karmāṇi  sthitibhāñji bhavanti | nahi  niśitataranakharakoṭividāritasamadakarikaraṭagalitamuktāphalanikara  parikara-prakāśitapratāpamahasi siṃhakiśorake guhāmadhitiṣṭhati  capalamanaso vidravaṇamātrabalaśālino hiraṇapotakāḥ svairaṃ  svavyāpārapariśīlanāpaṭubhāvamavalambante iti | tameva śaraṇaṃ  gaccha-ityupakramya matprasādāt-iti nirvāhavākyamabhidadhadbhagavān  paramātmānamīśvaraṃ vāsudevaṃ caikatayā yojayatīti

plain_english: Thus this knowledge, more secret than secret, has been declared by me; examine it completely and act as you wish.
sanskrit_cite: iti te jñānamākhyātaṃ guhyādguhyataraṃ mayā | vimṛśyaitadaśeṣeṇa yathecchasi tathā kuru | tadevedaṃ jñānamuktam | guhyāt-vedāntādapi  guhyam-paramādvaitaprakāśanāt | etaccāśeṣeṇa  vimṛśyeti-tātparyamatra vicāryetyarthaḥ | tacca tātparyaṃ  yathāvasaramasmābhiḥ śṛṅgrāhikayaiva prakāśitaṃ yadyapi  tathāpi sphuṭamaśeṣavimarśanaṃ pradarśyate-upādeyatamaṃ hyadaḥ | nāsminnirūpyamāṇe śrūyamāṇe vā matistṛpyati

plain_english: Hear again my supreme word, most secret of all; because you are dear to me, I will speak what is beneficial.
sanskrit_cite: guhyatamaṃ yadatra niścitam tajjñānamidānīṃ śṛṇu-ityāha   sarvaguhyatamaṃ bhūyaḥ śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ | iṣṭo'si me  dṛḍhamatistato vakṣyāmi te hitam

plain_english: Be of mind fixed on me, be my devotee, worship me, bow to me; you will come to me alone.
sanskrit_cite: manmanā bhava madbhakto madyājī māṃ namaskuru | māmevaiṣyasi  satyaṃ te pratijāne priyo'si me | manmanā bhava-ityādinā śāstre brahmārpaṇa eva sarvathā  prādhānyam-iti niścitam | brahmārpaṇakāriṇaḥ  śāstramidamarthavadityuktam | āha ca-

plain_english: Abandoning all dharmas, go to me alone as refuge; I will liberate you from all sins, do not grieve.
sanskrit_cite: sarvadharmānparityajya māmekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja | ahaṃ tvāṃ  sarvapāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ | sarvadharmāniti | yadidaṃ yuddhakaraṇe prāsaṅgikabandhuvadhādi  tasya sarvasyāhaṃ kartā-ityātmadharmatāṃ  parityajya-tathācāryādihananakriyāniṣedhe mama dharmo  bhaviṣyati-iti manasā vihāya | māmevaikaṃ sarvakartāraṃ  parameśvaraṃ svatantraṃ śaraṇaṃ sarvasvabhāvādhiṣṭhāyakatayā  vraja | ata evāhaṃ sarvajñaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpebhyastvāṃ  mokṣayiṣyāmīti | mā śucaḥ-kiṃkartavyatāmohaṃ mā gāḥ

plain_english: This knowledge is not to be spoken to the unqualified; secrecy preserves its success, and envy toward the Lord is disrespect.
sanskrit_cite: idaṃ te nātapaskāya nābhaktāya kadācana | na cāśuśrūṣave  vācyaṃ na ca māṃ yo'bhyasūyati | asya jñānasya gopyamānatvaṃ siddhidam-sarvajanāviṣayatvāt | tapasā tāvatpāpagranthau viśīrṇe kuśalaparipākonmukhatā bhavati | iti pūrvaṃ tapaḥ tapasaḥ śraddhā jāyate | saivātra bhaktiḥ | śraddhāpyupajātā kadācinna prarohati-saudāmanīva  kṣaṇadṛṣṭanaṣṭatvāt | tatastatprarohe śrotumicchā bhavati | iyadapi ca kasyacidanīśvare vastuni śuṣkasāṃkhyādijñāne bhavati | seśvare'pi vā kasyacitphalārthitayā phalameva pradhānīkṛtya  bhagavantaṃ ca svātmānaṃ tadupakaraṇapātrīkaraṇena nyakkṛtya  bhavet | yaduktaṃ   puruṣaśca karmārthatvāt karmāṇyapi phalārthatvāt | (pū0 mī0  sū0)   iti | evamubhayathāpi bhagavatyasūyaivānādara ityarthaḥ

plain_english: Whoever declares this supreme secret among devotees, making supreme devotion to the Lord, comes to the Lord without doubt.
sanskrit_cite: ya idaṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ madbhakteṣvabhidhāsyati | bhaktiṃ mayi  parāṃ kṛtvā māmevaiṣyatyasaṃśayaḥ | bhaktimiti-etadeva mayi bhaktikaraṇaṃ yadbhakteṣvetannirūpaṇam | abhidhāsyati-ābhimukhyena śāstroktaprakriyayā  dhāsyati-vitariṣyati | sa manmayatāmetīti vidhirevaiṣa  nārthavādaḥ | evamanyatra

plain_english: No one among men will be a greater doer of what is dear to me, and no one else on earth is dearer.
sanskrit_cite: na ca tasmānmanuṣyeṣu kaścinme priyakṛttamaḥ | bhavitā na ca me  tasmādanyaḥ priyataro bhuvi

plain_english: Whoever studies this righteous dialogue of ours is worshipped by me through knowledge-sacrifice; this is my thought.
sanskrit_cite: adhyeṣyate ca ya imaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃvādamāvayoḥ | jñānayajñena  tenāhamiṣṭaḥ syāmiti me matiḥ

plain_english: A faithful, non-envious man who hears this is also liberated and attains the auspicious worlds of meritorious acts.
sanskrit_cite: śraddhāvānanasūyaśca śṛṇuyādapi yo naraḥ | so'pi muktaḥ  śubhāṃllokānprāpnuyātpuṇyakarmaṇām

plain_english: Has this been heard by you, O son of Pṛthā, with one-pointed mind? Has ignorance-delusion been destroyed for you, O winner of wealth?
sanskrit_cite: kaccidetacchrutaṃ pārtha tvayaikāgreṇa cetasā | kaccidajñānasammohaḥ pranaṣṭaste dhanañjaya

plain_english: Arjuna says his delusion is gone, memory is gained by Krishna's grace, he stands free of doubt, and will do Krishna's word; the commentary notes that war-readiness has arisen, though full brahman-knowledge has not yet arisen.
sanskrit_cite: arjuna uvāca   naṣṭo mohaḥ smṛtirlabdhā tvatprasādānmayā'cyuta | sthito'smi  gatasandehaḥ kariṣye vacanaṃ tava | naṣṭo mohaḥ-ityādinā yuddhapravṛttistāvadarjunasyotpannā natu  samyagbrahma-vittvaṃ jātam-iti  sūcayanbhāvino'nugītārthasyāvakāśaṃ dadāti

plain_english: Sanjaya says he heard this wondrous, hair-raising dialogue between Vasudeva's son and the great-souled Partha.
sanskrit_cite: sañjaya uvāca   ityahaṃ vāsudevasya pārthasya ca mahātmanaḥ | saṃvādamimamaśrauṣamadbhutaṃ romaharṣaṇam

plain_english: By Vyasa's grace he heard this more secret great yoga, spoken directly by Krishna, lord of yoga, himself.
sanskrit_cite: vyāsaprasādācchrutavānetadguhyataraṃ mahat | yogaṃ  yogīśvarātkṛṣṇātsākṣātkathayataḥ svayam

plain_english: O king, remembering again and again the wondrous, meritorious dialogue of Kesava and Arjuna, I rejoice again and again.
sanskrit_cite: rājan saṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya saṃvādamimamadbhutam | keśavārjunayoḥ puṇyaṃ hṛṣyāmi ca punaḥ punaḥ

plain_english: And remembering again and again Hari's most wondrous form, wonder arises in me, O great king; I rejoice greatly again and again.
sanskrit_cite: tacca saṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya rūpamatyudbhutaṃ hareḥ | vismayo me  mahārāja prahṛṣye ca punaḥ punaḥ

plain_english: Where Krishna, lord of yoga, and Partha, bow-bearer, are, there are splendor, victory, certain prosperity, and policy; Sanjaya gathers the dialogue in firm order, and mere remembrance of it is said to give supreme Brahman, so that by mere remembrance of the Lord-Arjuna dialogue, through attainment of reality, splendor, victory, and powers arise.
sanskrit_cite: yatra yogīśvaraḥ kṛṣṇo yatra pārtho dhanurdharaḥ | tatra  śrīrvijayo bhūtirdhruvā nītirmatirmama | saṃjayavacanena saṃvādamupasaṃharannetadarthasya  gāḍhaprabandhakrameṇa nirantaracintāsantānopakṛtanairyantaryādeva  cānte suparisphuṭanirvikalpānubhavarūpatāmāpādyamānaṃ  smaraṇamātrameva parabrahmapradāyakam-ityucyate | evaṃ  bhagavadarjunasaṃvādamātrasmaraṇādeva tattvāvāptyā  śrīvijayavibhūtaya iti śivam

plain_english: Here is the summary verse: breaking the dark intellect, attaining Viṣṇu beyond discrimination, all becomes Śaṅkara; the eighteenth chapter of the Gītārthasaṃgraha composed by Abhinavagupta is complete, and Śiva is praised.
sanskrit_cite: atra saṃgrahaślokaḥ   bhaṅktvā jñānavimohamantharamayīṃ sattvādibhinnāṃ dhiyaṃ  prāpya svātmavibhūtasundaratayā viṣṇuṃ vikalpātigam | yaktiṃcitsvarasodyadindriyanijavyāpāramātrasthite- rhelātaḥ kurute  tadasya sakalaṃ saṃpadyate śaṅkaram | iti śrīmahāmaheśvarācāryavaryarājānakābhinavaguptapādaviracite  śrīmadbhagavadgītārthasaṃgrahe'ṣṭādaśo'dhyāyaḥ | śrīmānkātyāyano'bhūdvararucisadṛśaḥ  prasphuradbodhatṛpta-stadvaṃśālaṅkṛto yaḥ  sthiramatirabhavatsauśukākhyo'tividvān | vipraḥ śrī  bhūtirājastadanu samabhavattasya sūnurmahātmā yenāmī  sarvalokāstamasi nipatitāḥ proddhṛtā bhānuneva | taccaraṇakamalamadhupo bhagavadgītārthasaṃgrahaṃ vyadadhāt | abhinavaguptaḥ saddivajaloṭakakṛtacodanāvaśataḥ | ata idamayathārthaṃ vā yathārthamapi sarvathā naiva | viduṣāmasūyanīyaṃ kṛtyamidaṃ bāndhavārthaṃ hi | abhinavarūpā śaktistadgupto yo maheśvaro devaḥ | tadubhayayāmalarūpamabhinavaguptaṃ śivaṃ vande | paripūrṇo'yaṃ śrīmadbhagavadgītārthasaṃgrahaḥ | kṛtistrinayanacaraṇasaroruha cintanalabdhaprasiddherabhinavaguptasyeti  śivam
